close_reason: Rewrote test docstring at metadata.rs:859-869 to make clear the test validates handler error-routing plumbing, not backend §3.1 uniqueness logic. Added cross-references to the real §3.1 semantics tests at memory::tests::uniqueness_constraint_enforced and tests/metadata_tests.rs::set_create_duplicate_returns_already_exists.
description:
What is unclear: metadata.rs:692 (set_create_uniqueness_violation_returns_already_exists) has the docstring 'Oracle: §3.1 — uniqueness violation produces alreadyExists in notCreated. The handler is generic — the backend reports the constraint via BackendSetError::SetError.'

The test does NOT exercise uniqueness logic. It calls backend.force_create_error(...) to inject an alreadyExists SetError, then asserts the handler routes it to notCreated. This is a test of the HANDLER's error-routing plumbing, not of §3.1 semantics. The §3.1 reference in the docstring is misleading.

Audience: contributor reading this test to understand how §3.1 uniqueness works. They will conclude the handler enforces §3.1, when actually the backend does — and this test is unable to validate the backend's logic.

What would make it clear: rewrite the docstring as 'Oracle: RFC 8620 §5.3 — when the backend reports alreadyExists via BackendSetError::SetError, the handler routes it into notCreated[create_id]. This test validates the handler's plumbing, not the backend's §3.1 logic. See memory.rs::tests::uniqueness_constraint_enforced for the §3.1 semantics test against the reference backend.'
title: Test docstring 'Oracle: §3.1 — uniqueness violation produces alreadyExists' is misleading — test uses force_create_error injection, not real uniqueness logic
